summary: Supports KiCad 10.0 and later. Tested up to KiCad 10.99, the KiCad 11 development line. No KiCad version is known to break it, so there is no maximum.

verified.checked: Connect over the IPC API, search, import an LCSC part with easyeda2kicad, register it in the project library tables, and load the result with kicad-cli.
The same, and KiCad's own user interface discovering the plugin action and starting the application.

fields.minimum: The oldest KiCad this build is declared to work with. Older is a refusal: the updater will not install this release under it, and the bootstrap will not download it. KiCad 9 and earlier have never been run against this project, which is why the minimum is 10.0 and not lower.
fields.tested_up_to: The newest KiCad this build was exercised against. Newer is a warning, never a refusal - 'tested up to' is not 'known broken'.
fields.maximum: null when no KiCad version is known to break this build, which is the case today. When it is set it is a hard limit: the updater and the bootstrap refuse, and the Plugin and Content Manager metadata carries it as kicad_version_max, which hides the package from a newer KiCad.
fields.versions: major.minor, or major.minor.patch. A missing patch reads as 0 in minimum and as 999 in tested_up_to and maximum, which is how KiCad's own Plugin and Content Manager compares these numbers.

read_by: .github/workflows/release.yml - writes kicad_version and kicad_version_max into the Plugin and Content Manager metadata from this file, and publishes this file as a release asset.
plugin/importer_launcher.py - reads the copy published with a release before downloading ~200 MB of application.

src/importer/KiCadUltra/Services/KiCadCompatibility.cs - the copy shipped beside the executable is what the About window reports; the copy published with a candidate release is what the updater checks before it downloads.
